questions.prompt: Which keyword is used to declare an interface in C#?
questions.explanation: Interfaces are declared using the 'interface' keyword. They define a contract of members without implementation.

questions.prompt: By default, interface members are implicitly _____ and _____.
questions.explanation: Interface members are implicitly public and abstract. You cannot use access modifiers on interface members.

questions.prompt: Can a class implement multiple interfaces in C#?
options: Only if they are in the same namespace
questions.explanation: C# supports multiple interface implementation via comma-separated interface names after the colon.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: class Dog : _____, _____
What is a key difference between an interface and an abstract class?
options: Interfaces cannot contain method implementations (before C# 8)
questions.explanation: Interfaces define only member signatures (prior to C# 8 default implementations), while abstract classes can provide concrete implementations.

questions.prompt: Arrange the correct interface declaration and implementation.
Which of the following can an interface contain in C# (pre-C# 8)?
questions.explanation: Interfaces can declare methods, properties, events, and indexers, but not fields, constructors, or destructors.

questions.prompt: Declare an interface ILogger with a Log method, and implement it in a ConsoleLogger class.
Fill in the blank to implement two interfaces.
When should you prefer an interface over an abstract class?
options: When you need multiple inheritance of type
questions.explanation: Interfaces allow a class to inherit behavior from multiple sources, solving the single-inheritance limitation of abstract classes.
